title: Chiral Transfer and Entanglement Generation of Even-Parity Bell States with Engineered Two-Photon Loss
authors: Lin Xiao, Jian Li, Mu Zhou, Bin Wei, Qing-Xu Li, Jia-Ji Zhu
abstract: We investigate chiral transfer and dissipative generation of even-parity Bell states in a two-qubit system with coherent two-photon driving and engineered two-photon loss. We find that adiabatic encirclement of a second-order exceptional point induces direction-dependent transfer between the Bell states $|Φ^+\rangle$ and $|Φ^-\rangle$, governed by a time-integrated low-loss branch-selection mechanism. We develop a hybrid-Liouvillian description with a control parameter $q$ that interpolates between conditional no-jump dynamics and unconditional Lindblad evolution, and use it to assess how exceptional-point-induced chirality survives in the presence of quantum jumps. When the same parameter loop is initialized in the separable state $|00\rangle$, it directly generates strong even-parity entanglement. Together, these results extend dissipative Bell-state control beyond the single-excitation manifold. They further demonstrate that exceptional-point-based protocols can unify chiral state transfer and entanglement generation within a single engineered two-photon platform.
summary: This paper details a method to control even-parity Bell states in a two-qubit system using engineered two-photon loss. By adiabatically encircling an exceptional point, the system exhibits chiral state transfer between $|\Phi^+angle$ and $|\Phi^-angle$. Crucially, the same engineered process simultaneously generates strong even-parity entanglement, unifying two key quantum control mechanisms.
main_problem: The research aims to extend chiral state transfer and dissipative entanglement generation protocols from odd-parity to even-parity Bell states in a two-qubit system.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that adiabatically encircling a second-order exceptional point induces chiral transfer between $|\Phi^+angle$ and $|\Phi^-angle$, and that the same loop can deterministically generate strong even-parity entanglement from a separable state.
method: The dynamics are analyzed using a hybrid Liouvillian description, which interpolates between conditional no-jump dynamics and standard Lindblad evolution, coupled with the theoretical framework of non-Hermitian physics.
model_or_system: The system is a two-qubit platform driven by coherent two-photon processes and engineered two-photon loss. The dynamics are confined to the even-parity subspace, which is structurally protected by parity symmetry.
key_observables: Bell-state fidelity ($F_{|\Phi^\pmangle}$), Concurrence ($C(ho)$), and the chiral contrast ($\Delta F$).
important_parameters: The recycling parameter $q \in [0, 1]$, the driving period $T$, and the engineered two-photon loss rate $\kappa$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Markov approximation, and the structural protection of the even-parity subspace is key to robustness.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Bloch-sphere representation of the even-parity subspace, the parameter loops used to encircle the EP, and the time evolution of fidelity and concurrence as a function of the loop parameters.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical model and the effective Hamiltonian in the even-parity subspace. It then introduces the hybrid Liouvillian dynamics to analyze the interplay between chiral transfer (via EP encirclement) and entanglement generation, comparing the conditional ($q=0$) and unconditional ($q=1$) limits.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, engineered platform demonstrating how non-Hermitian physics (EPs) can be harnessed to perform fundamental quantum information tasks (state transfer and entanglement) in a robust, dissipative manner.
